comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that gain decreases at ~0.02 R*/rod/s corresponding to behavioral threshold changes. OpenEval provides detailed technical support from Figure 3, while peer reviewers affirm this as a systematic experimental demonstration. High agreement on this central claim.

Both support the fluctuating background experiment and rapid gain changes. OpenEval emphasizes the mean vs. variance distinction (C3, C4, C36) and kinetics (C78), while peer reviewers focus on rapid adaptation and single-photon sensitivity (C39-C44, C78). Overlapping claims with different emphasis but consistent support.

Both support the rapid kinetics and spatial pooling findings. OpenEval focuses on gain kinetics and rod integration calculations (C39-C44), while peer reviewers affirm rapid adaptation at AII amacrine cells with photon absorption in hundreds of rods. Strong agreement on temporal dynamics.

Both support the spatial adaptation experiments showing complete transfer at 50 μm and incomplete at larger widths (C45-C49). OpenEval provides detailed technical support from Figures 7-8, while peer reviewers accept this as part of systematic experimental demonstration. High agreement.

Both support localization to AII amacrine cells. OpenEval emphasizes no transfer from rod to cone pathways (C50-C54, C66) with multiple experimental constraints, while peer reviewers directly affirm adaptation occurs at the level of AII amacrine cells. Strong agreement on localization.

Minor overlap on C50 regarding spatial pooling requirements. OpenEval groups this with pathway localization evidence, while peer reviewers include it with spatial adaptation experiments. Both support the claim but in different contexts.

Both address gain and noise measurements from Figure 3, but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds claims C25-C32 well-supported with clear data, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about terminology, requesting clearer definitions of 'gain', 'noise', and 'background' and questioning multiple gain measures. Disagreement on clarity rather than validity.

Both address spike responses vs. excitatory currents (C16-C19). OpenEval notes support but acknowledges missing inhibitory input data weakens conclusions. Peer reviewers critique lack of precision ('how small?') and request quantitative descriptions. Both express some uncertainty, though OpenEval is more supportive overall.

Both support the integration of multiple gain control mechanisms (C71-C75). OpenEval finds the hierarchy well-supported with appropriate citations and smooth function demonstrated. Peer reviewers affirm the systematic nature and high significance. Strong agreement, with peer reviewers also accepting the evolutionary interpretation (C76).

Both address threshold changes and post-retinal contributions (C61-C62). OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 3F though notes speculation about post-retinal contributions. Peer reviewers accept the comparison to psychophysical experiments without challenge. Agreement on support.

Both address the main conclusion about gain control at physical limits (C77, C81). OpenEval synthesizes multiple findings to support this conclusion. Peer reviewers affirm this as part of the core systematic demonstration. Strong agreement on this high-level conclusion.
Minor overlap on C78 regarding rapid kinetics. OpenEval includes this in the physical limit synthesis, while peer reviewers include it in the rapid adaptation finding. Both support the claim.

Both address evolutionary interpretation (C76). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting the claim is speculative without comparative/evolutionary evidence. Peer reviewers accept it as part of the high-significance systematic findings without critique. Disagreement on the strength of this speculative claim.

Both address background on rod bipolar pathway and On parasol cells (C10-C15). OpenEval finds these well-cited and appropriately supported. Peer reviewers request better presentation and rationalization of cell choice, indicating uncertainty about clarity rather than validity. Mild disagreement on presentation quality.

Both address methodological details (C82-C84). OpenEval finds these clearly stated and appropriate. Peer reviewers implicitly accept methods through enthusiasm for systematic experiments. Strong agreement on methods.

OpenEval rates C67-C68 as uncertain due to missing data for midget cells, though anatomical logic is sound. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about pathway anatomy and missing midget cell data.

OpenEval rates C56-C57 as uncertain due to reliance on unpublished data for spontaneous activation rate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about rod noise comparisons.

OpenEval finds C20-C22 (psychophysical background) well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do affirm successful comparison to psychophysics generally.

OpenEval finds C63-C65 (comparison to prior mechanisms) well-supported for establishing novelty. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about how the mechanism differs from prior work.
OpenEval finds C5-C7 (motivating examples for gain control importance) well-supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory motivation claims.
OpenEval finds C8-C9 (background on rod sensitivity and noise) well-cited and accurate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
OpenEval finds C29, C37 (Poisson predictions) theoretically sound and correctly derived. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific theoretical predictions.

OpenEval finds C38 (slow baseline changes) supported by Figure 5 supplement, important for understanding temporal dynamics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific observation.
OpenEval finds C58-C60 (citations comparing measurement approaches) accurate and appropriately contextualized. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature comparisons.
OpenEval finds C69-C70 (RGC properties motivating multiple mechanisms) well-established and accurate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
